BiblicalUsage: çâgân means a prefect of a province, and the Bible means it plainly. It occurs 16 times in the Old Testament, in Ezekiel and Ezra and elsewhere, and none of those places bends the word out of shape. What it says in one place is what it says in all of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe çâgân earns its place. A prefect of a province is the kind of thing God repeats because His people need to hear it more than once.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
